name: Denmark: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: the Denmark package as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: K1 recruitment and informed-consent procedure present on EU template v2.0 (or the same information in an accepted location), with a section for every population pathway in the plan.
K2 recruitment material present for every recruitment tool, as presented; audio or video as a storyboard.
For every population in population_sets whose trigger is true: one L1 participant information sheet and one blank L1 consent form, with the same version and date.

Every population-specific consent document needed by the protocol is included (parents, 12-14, 15-17, representative, limited capacity, emergency, witness, pregnancy, optional substudy, secondary data use, right not to know, parental power of attorney where used).
Participant information and consent forms are in Danish for the normal Danish-speaking population; validated translations are prepared if a participant or representative will not understand Danish.
For every Danish site: M1 CV of the principal investigator only (unless another document is specifically requested), M2 declaration of interests, N1 site suitability.
O1 insurance information: Patienterstatningen coverage stated correctly, or independent insurance documented for sites outside that scheme.
P1 participant compensation description and P2 trial budget (draft or final), plus a draft CTA where that route is used.
Proof of fee uploaded only where the current invoice process asks for it.
R1 statement on the GDPR and the Danish Data Protection Act; relevant foreign transfers explained in the participant information.
S1 biological-sample information with type, amount, purpose, location, duration and disposition.

Material outside VMK's Part II approval (data-only pregnant-partner follow-up, extra samples for unspecified future research) is omitted from Part II, or if uploaded carries the VMK-required statements (DECISIONS.md D12, D13).
Sites, principal investigators and planned participant numbers in CTIS match M1, M2 and N1.
Every participant- or representative-facing document is in Danish (plus validated translations where needed).
Administrative documents are in Danish or English.

No participant, representative or investigator signatures on uploaded consent forms; documents are not signed merely because they are uploaded to CTIS; N1 issuer fields completed by the issuing person as the current EC form requires.

The recruitment and consent procedure identifies a Danish-authorised physician as the person giving oral information and receiving consent, and any delegated consent physician has a written agreement with the principal investigator.
Compensation amounts and conditions identical in P1, P2 where relevant, K2 and every participant document.
Insurance route (Patienterstatningen or independent insurance) identical in O1 and every participant document.
Sample types, amounts, locations, storage, transfers and retention identical in S1, the protocol and the participant documents.
Data flows, record access, recipients, transfers and retention identical in R1, the participant documents and the protocol.
Consent pathways and who obtains consent in K1 match the L1 sets and the protocol; patient-record screening and contact logic match the Danish requirements.
Documents adapted from the reference package contain all Danish national additions and no leftovers from the reference country.
items.applies_when: Denmark is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B-S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each document; the fee document in the CTIS area the authority instructs.
Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>, with only the fields that distinguish the document.
Version and date entered in CTIS metadata, not in the title; the filename does not rely on conflicting date or version information.
Personal names only where disclosure permits (principal investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished.
Uploaded filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
No document is duplicated across CTIS sections without a clear reason.
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: Denmark receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables (revised CTIS transparency rules from 18 June 2024; ACT EU guidance v2.2, 30 April 2026).

Publishable documents: personal data and CCI identified separately; public version redacts only qualifying material, irreversibly and unsearchably; author metadata removed; signatures never disclosed.
Public and assessment versions differ only by the intended redactions; each in the correct CTIS slot.
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
The patient-facing set passed the Denmark release check (participant QC C10).
